subsystems.name: Transducer array
subsystems.role: generates the ultrasound beam and steers it electronically to a deep target.
parts: piezoelectric elements (lead zirconate titanate or single-crystal)

subsystems.name: Drive electronics
subsystems.role: generate the shaped electrical pulses delivered to each element.

subsystems.name: Targeting and acoustic modelling
subsystems.role: works out where the beam actually lands after the skull distorts it.

subsystems.name: Coupling and positioning
subsystems.role: gets sound into the head without air gaps and holds the array in place.

subsystems.name: Monitoring and safety interlocks
subsystems.role: detects unwanted heating or neural effects and stops delivery.

subsystems.name: Protocol and control software
subsystems.role: defines pulse patterns and enforces limits on intensity and duty cycle.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the array
buildSteps.detail: Piezoelectric material is diced into many elements, wired individually, and potted into a housing that fits against the scalp.

buildSteps.title: Characterise the beam
buildSteps.detail: The array is scanned in a water tank to map its pressure field, focal size and sidelobes at each steering setting.

buildSteps.title: Model the individual skull
buildSteps.detail: A CT scan gives skull thickness and density; software simulates how much the bone slows, absorbs and bends the beam.

buildSteps.title: Correct the phases
buildSteps.detail: Each element's phase and amplitude are adjusted so the distorted waves still arrive in step at the chosen target.

buildSteps.title: Register and position
buildSteps.detail: The array is aligned to the patient's MRI using neuronavigation, then coupled to the scalp with gel or a hydrogel pad.

buildSteps.title: Select a dose
buildSteps.detail: Frequency, intensity, pulse length, duty cycle and train duration are chosen low enough to be non-thermal but strong enough to shift neuronal activity.

buildSteps.title: Deliver and monitor
buildSteps.detail: Pulses are delivered in short trains while EEG and device readouts watch for unintended effects or heating.

buildSteps.title: Verify the effect
buildSteps.detail: Change in brain activity is checked by functional imaging or electrophysiology, and the result is compared against a sham condition.

prerequisites.why: they allow electronic steering of a focus through the skull without moving the device.
bone distorts and absorbs the beam, so targeting depends on CT-based modelling that is still imperfect.
MRI and CT are needed to pick and verify a deep target.
the mechanism is thought to involve membrane displacement and channels such as Piezo1, but details at the doses used remain unsettled.

prerequisites.tech: Dosimetry and safety standards for neuromodulation
prerequisites.why: standards exist for diagnostic imaging and ablation, not for repeated low-intensity brain stimulation.

pathway.milestone: small human trials targeting deep structures such as the thalamus, hippocampus and prefrontal cortex
pathway.unlocks: evidence that the technique can change activity in chosen circuits safely.

pathway.milestone: larger sham-controlled trials for depression, epilepsy and chronic pain
pathway.unlocks: separation of real effect from placebo and confirmation of parameter sets.

pathway.milestone: closed-loop systems that read brain activity and adjust the beam automatically
regulatory clearance for a neuromodulation indication
pathway.unlocks: clinical adoption; high-intensity ultrasound ablation of deep brain targets is already clinically used for tremor, which de-risks the delivery hardware.
